venue: Ben Hill Griffin Stadium, Gainesville FL
title: Week 1 vs FAU
dek: Faulkner never lets you sit on Baugh. White never lets the tackle know who is coming from the outside. FAU still moved the chains on the short throw Florida left open.
watchNote: PROVISIONAL — Copilot rhythm + plain words. Combined tape + GNFP. Fan rail stays empty until Charles approves.
headline: Baugh is the night. Faulkner’s job is to keep you from putting extra men on him. Woods is how White messes with the tackle.

offense.body:
You cannot put a card on this offense. That is the point.

Faulkner is not installing a system you can memorize. He asks a new question before you finish the last one. Same start. Different answer. They can still go the other way without changing the play.

If you creep up for Baugh, he throws the short one to Brown. First man misses. Forty-nine yards. People will remember a long touchdown. It was a short throw and a missed tackle.

If you follow the two tackles who look like they are leading a run, the ball goes the other way — to Brown — and the three linemen in the middle are already out in front of him. Later it is Clark, same idea. On the 10-yard score those big people are already down the field.

If you stay put and play Baugh, he runs it. He scores from 12 with those same linemen actually leading him this time. In the third quarter the whole stadium knows it is Baugh, and he still goes 61.

That is one idea. He keeps changing the picture.

He lines the receivers way out wide, and sometimes he puts Brown and Wilson one behind the other. FAU kept extra people near Baugh because they have seen him. That leaves Brown or Wilson alone with half the field. One miss and he is gone. That is Brown’s night — the short throw, the screen, the 14, the 33. He is not a trick-play guy.

More players on one side, then a man in motion, and they can still go the other way. FAU was still counting when the ball was snapped. That is not decoration. That is how Faulkner plays the numbers.

The fake run is the lie and the truth. Sometimes the tackles take off and the ball goes with the three in the middle — Brown, later Clark. Sometimes those tackles really are leading Baugh, and he walks into it. When they need one yard, nobody leaves — sneak, Philo from the 3.

They will also have a tackle take off like it is a run when they are passing. The rusher is paid to chase Philo. If he honors the fake, the rush dies and nobody blocked him. If he chases Philo, the other side is empty. Week one they showed that more than they got a big play out of it. They will hand it off from that same look. Remember it.

Philo with Baugh right behind him showed up once — they ran it, then they faked it and Wilson sat in the open grass for 19. One look. Not the offense. Wilson moved the chains all night. He sits in the grass you leave him.

Philo ran the offense. In and out. Eyes down when they rushed him. Step up, still find somebody. He does not have to be the hero. Stockton finished a ball that was a little late and walked it in from 11. Abrams was on time — the deep one when FAU finally crowded Baugh and the line looked like pass, not run. Lead him a step and he walks in. The pick is Mays. The ball came off his hands. Sweeney was sitting. When Philo holds it, the play dies.

Baugh is the night. Fourteen for 160, three rushing scores, the 61. FAU filled every hole on some plays — extra people, nowhere to go — and he still ripped it or scored. That is not Faulkner winning those plays. That is the best player in the building. Faulkner’s job is to keep you from putting eleven on him. Receivers out wide make that a nightmare. Duke Clark is the change of pace. They will not run Baugh thirty times.

The line is clean — almost no penalties, no late-shift disaster like last year. They are also not getting out to the linebackers fast. The wide run they tried, they cannot run yet. Faulkner still shows it so you have to worry about the outside. What he does instead: he does not ask this line to block everybody. He leaves people unblocked on purpose. The snaps over Philo’s head are Harrison Moore’s hands. Sumrall already said that. The one that lost twenty inside the five is the one that can lose a real game. Philo ran it himself once, FAU’s end was still there, lost two. The idea was fine. They lost the play.

They block down the field like they mean it. Ten becomes thirty. Micah Jones blows up one man, then the next, and they throw him the last one. That is not a coincidence. Get a big person in front of a skill player. Same idea as Clark’s score.

Saturday was a coordinator who flexes to what you are weak at, a back you cannot tackle if they do not put extra men on him, and a quarterback who ran the offense. Clean the snap, the play Philo ran and lost, and the ball off Mays. The rest is a headache you have to prepare for.
bullets: You creep up for Baugh, he throws the short one to Brown. That is the 49.
You follow the fake, the ball goes the other way — Brown, later Clark.
You stay put, Baugh runs it. The 12 and the 61.
Clean the snap, the play Philo ran and lost, and the ball off Mays.

defense.body:
FAU wants to throw it short until you step up and take that throw away. Everybody knows that. Florida left that throw on the grass.

Corners lined up yards off. Linebackers did not step into the short area. You showed them something before the snap and then gave them that first throw anyway. Ninety plays. They were 10-of-13 on third at one point. Henry and Valsin took what was given. Sumrall said it out loud: third-and-1, you cannot have your corner nine yards off. That happened. That is what ninety plays cost.

White will live with the five-to-eight yard throw if they tackle. They did not tackle enough of it, and nobody was standing where that ball lands, so it became a night.

He still has a real idea. He moves people. Woods is how he does it. On third down White moves him. Sometimes Woods is the man rushing from the outside. Sometimes he walks inside and somebody else has that outside rush. The tackle never knows who is coming. Mix it. Often.

When Veltkamp holds it, that idea pays. Coleman acts like the middle is open, the ball goes outside, Coleman is already there. That pick is bait. Not a blitz. He moved the quarterback’s eyes. He tips the next one. Johnson goes up and gets it. Same idea. Bett later beats the quarterback at the 1. Ball out. Johnson falls on it. McCloud stops them on fourth-and-2. The rush finally finishes.

Safeties were the clean part — Coleman, Thornton. Clark played a real night in the slot and lost one ball to the corner of the end zone with no help over the top. That throw is the other side of lining up yards off. Valsin, 20. Same play Stockton ran the other way.

What leaked is the stuff they agreed to give, plus the jobs inside it. The pile at the 1 — they had enough people, they lost the yard. The man on the outside left and Veltkamp walked in from 7. Woods is supposed to stay there. When he chases, FAU ran at him. Keep him there.

Later they sent four rushers and still played the corners off. That takes away the deep ball. It also leaves the short throw and the throw to the corner alive.

They were ready for how fast FAU plays. They were not staring at the sideline when it snapped. Veltkamp is a real quarterback — he can throw it and he can run it. Sumrall called the defense atrocious at times because ninety plays and those fourth downs are what you get when the short throw is free.

Stand where that short ball lands. Keep Woods on the outside when the quarterback runs it. Mix Woods. Make him hold it. Coleman already showed you what that looks like.
bullets: The short throw was open. That is why FAU ran 90 plays.
White moves Woods so the tackle never knows who is coming.
When Veltkamp holds it, Coleman and Johnson take it.
Fix the pile, the man on the outside, and the throw to the corner.

specials.body: The drive stalls. They take the points. Durkin from 53. Florida never punts. FAU’s 18-yard punt is how the second Florida score starts.
bullets: FAU’s 18-yard punt sets up the short field.

keys: Faulkner never lets you sit on Baugh. You creep up, he throws the short one. You follow the fake, the ball goes the other way. You play it straight, Baugh runs it.
Receivers out wide force a bad choice: extra men on Baugh, or room for Brown.
White moves Woods so the tackle cannot get comfortable. FAU still moved the chains because the short throw was open.
When Veltkamp holds it, Coleman and Johnson take it. Fix the pile, the man on the outside, and the throw to the corner.

nextWeek.look: They will throw it short and the quarterback will run it. Sixkiller is their guy. Florida will still hand it to Baugh and keep changing the picture. White has to stand on that short throw and keep Woods on the outside when Sixkiller runs it himself.
